_comment: ID ledger for the MOBA generators -- read by apps/moba/id_alloc.py. Every custom ID this fork assigns belongs to exactly one owner's block. Two owners must NEVER share a block: generators window-clear their blocks, so an overlap lets one wipe the other's rows. Namespaces are independent -- waypoint_data 900206 and creature_template 900206 are unrelated ids and both legal. A namespace names a table; the id is that table's primary key.

twisted_treeline.note: hand-assigned, nothing allocates here. 5000 = 'Twisted Treeline', AreaBit 3000. Stock AreaTable.dbc runs to id 4987 / AreaBit 3617, so both are clear. AreaBit is a separate id space -- it indexes the client's exploration bitmask, and reusing a stock one would mark another zone explored.

base_slot.note: hand-assigned in maps/*/base_config.yaml as battleground_template_id; gen_base.py window-clears the block. ONE number in three places: this row's ID, the BattlegroundTypeId enumerator in SharedDefines.h, and the BattlemasterList.dbc row id -- server copy in mod_moba_bg_map.sql, client copy written by apps/moba/wmo/dbc_tool.py. Deliberately NOT enumerated: an INACTIVE bundle may legally declare the same slot as the active one, so a reader would report a false collision -- gen_base.py's active_by_slot check is what enforces uniqueness. Stock BattlemasterList.dbc holds 1-11, 30 and 32; the block stops at 19 because an id of 32 or more breaks SetHolidayWeekends' `1 << bgtype`.

store.note: creature.guid, NOT an entry. gen_store.py spawns shopkeepers with guid == entry so the two read together, which is why these numbers match the creature_template/store block -- they are still unrelated ids in unrelated namespaces. The only static spawn rows the fork owns; towers, creeps, neutrals and domes are spawned from C++ and have no rows here.
hand-assigned in maps/*/store_config.yaml under shopkeeper.teams; the generated SQL clears the whole block

towers.note: auto-assigned; the record is maps/*/tower_config.lock.json. The second block was carved by id_alloc.py itself when map #2 filled the first -- BLOCK_SIZE is a flat 100, so 'the right second-block size' turned out not to be a decision.

base_spawn.note: hand-assigned in maps/*/base_config.yaml under spawn.<team>.graveyard_id; the generated SQL clears the whole block. Six-digit ids are safe here where map_dbc's are not -- GameGraveyard keeps an unordered_map, not an index array, so a high id costs one hash entry. Eye of the Storm's 1103/1104 were borrowed before this block existed and are NOT in it; mod_moba_restore_eots.sql put them back on map 566.

base_dome.note: hand-assigned in maps/*/base_config.yaml under spawn.dome; the generated SQL clears the whole block

item_copies.note: NOT a dense window: a copy's entry is its SOURCE entry + 900000, so this block is a sparse mirror of the whole stock item space. Nothing allocates here and there is nothing to enumerate -- the block exists so a future allocator cannot wander in. The client-patch drop-item copies will land here too, under the same offset.

twisted_treeline.note: hand-assigned, nothing allocates here. 900 = TwistedTreeline; stock Map.dbc tops out at 724. Deliberately NOT in the 900000 range every other block uses: DBCStorage sizes its index table to max(id)+1, so a six-digit map id costs ~7 MB of null pointers.

hand-assigned, nothing allocates here. 200 = map 900's only bracket; stock PvpDifficulty.dbc runs to id 108. Small ids for the same reason as map_dbc: DBCStorage sizes its index table to max(id)+1. RangeIndex is a different id space and is NOT covered by this block -- it is the bracket index, and must stay under MAX_BATTLEGROUND_BRACKETS (16) because BattlegroundQueue arrays are dimensioned by it. Two copies now: the server's row in mod_moba_bg_map.sql and the client's, written by dbc_tool.py. Both must carry the same MapID, RangeIndex and level range -- the client uses its copy to decide whether the PvP frame will let you queue at all.

hand-assigned, nothing allocates here. 800 = map 900's only difficulty row; stock MapDifficulty.dbc runs to id 753. Small ids for the same reason as map_dbc: DBCStorage sizes its index table to max(id)+1. Its absence is what made spawnMasks[900] zero, so every static spawn on the map logged a wrong-spawn-mask error.

creep_paths.note: auto-assigned in forward/reverse pairs; the record is maps/*/lane_config.lock.json. Mirrors lane_config.yaml's id_range, which stays the generator's own input until step 3 -- a second bundle declaring a different id_range would diverge from this block until then.

twisted_treeline.note: hand-assigned, nothing allocates here. Row ids only -- stock WMOAreaTable.dbc runs to 51118. The row's WMOID column is a different id space and is NOT covered by this block: it is MOHD.id, stamped inside the .wmo, held at 9000 by blender_staging_setup.py. It must stay <= 32767, because GetWMOAreaTableEntryByTripple narrows the key to int16.
